parent_v15.key_result: cost-world-specific adaptive policies remained exact and cost-efficient, but changing only REL/FP/KO family costs changed canonical first actions 1023 times

scientific_question: If the analyst does not know which predeclared measurement-cost world will apply, can one cost-blind adaptive relational policy remain exact with low regret across all cost worlds?

analysis_base.measurements: unchanged REL, FP and KO atomic actions from v13-v15

policy_information.observed: measurement outcomes and the resulting surviving ecological-world subset

oracle_reference.definition: for each row, target and cost world, use the exact v15 adaptive minimum worst-case cost when that cost world is known in advance
oracle_reference.role: cost-specific lower bound used only to calculate regret

cost_blind_policy.tree_cost_vector: for each policy tree, one worst-case total cost is computed under each of the four cost worlds
cost_blind_policy.regret_vector: policy worst-case cost in cost world c minus the v15 cost-world-specific oracle minimum for c
cost_blind_policy.primary_objective: minimize maximum absolute regret across the four cost worlds
cost_blind_policy.exact_solver: enumerate exact adaptive policy cost vectors by dynamic programming over survivor subsets and prune componentwise dominated vectors before root minimax-regret selection

comparators.equal_cost_commitment: the canonical v15 equal-cost optimal adaptive tree, evaluated unchanged under all four cost worlds
comparators.cost_world_oracles: the four v15 cost-specific adaptive optima

predeclared_hypotheses.statement: Every row-target combination has at least one exact adaptive tree whose action choices are independent of cost-world identity.
predeclared_hypotheses.failure_rule: Any unresolved row-target combination refutes U1.

predeclared_hypotheses.statement: For every selected cost-blind policy and cost world, its worst-case total cost is >= the v15 oracle optimum for that same row, target and cost world.
predeclared_hypotheses.failure_rule: Any negative regret is an implementation/theory failure.

predeclared_hypotheses.statement: At least one row-target combination has minimum achievable maximum regret >0 when one policy must be shared across all four cost worlds.
predeclared_hypotheses.failure_rule: REFUTED if a zero-regret common policy exists for every row-target.

predeclared_hypotheses.statement: At least one row-target combination has a single exact adaptive policy that is simultaneously oracle-optimal in all four cost worlds.
predeclared_hypotheses.failure_rule: REFUTED if every row-target has positive irreducible regret.

predeclared_hypotheses.statement: At least one row-target combination has strictly lower maximum cross-cost regret under the minimax-regret policy than under committing to the v15 equal-cost optimal policy.
predeclared_hypotheses.failure_rule: REFUTED if equal-cost commitment is minimax-regret optimal everywhere.

predeclared_hypotheses.statement: At least one row-target minimax-regret policy has a different canonical first action from the v15 equal-cost oracle policy.
predeclared_hypotheses.failure_rule: REFUTED if the canonical first action never changes.

predeclared_hypotheses.statement: At least one row has minimax-regret policy maximum total cost for intervention or critical_node_count strictly below that for full_topology_identity.
predeclared_hypotheses.failure_rule: REFUTED if full topology is never more costly under the robust cost-blind policy.

predeclared_hypotheses.statement: Across the 144 rows and declared targets, more than one canonical first action appears among minimax-regret policies.
predeclared_hypotheses.failure_rule: REFUTED if one action is canonical first everywhere.

secondary_outputs: distribution of minimum maximum regret by target
fraction of row-targets with zero regret
cost-world regret vectors of selected policies
maximum total-cost overhead relative to knowing the cost world
rows where cost uncertainty changes measurement count as well as measurement family
Pareto-frontier size of undominated cost vectors at the root
claim_boundary: The four cost worlds remain synthetic analyst scenarios rather than field budgets.
Minimax regret is one robust-choice criterion and is not claimed as universally optimal for field design.
The solver is generic finite decision-tree optimization; the ecological contribution is the robustness of EOG relational evidence recommendations to cost-world uncertainty.
No fifth cost world or post-score cost calibration is allowed.
stop_rules: Do not change regret from absolute to relative after scoring.
Do not add priors over cost worlds after scoring.
Do not change the four v15 cost worlds.
Do not replace minimax regret with expected cost after scoring.
